title: Charles Elcock: raw material, preparation practice, Type Slide commerce, and surviving workshop archive
core_result: The Elcock case now closes a rare nineteenth-century chain from collectable/raw foraminiferal material and documented manipulation, through public reputation and a standardized priced Type Slide product distributed by named agents, to a surviving personal workshop archive containing Type Slide drawers, retained slides, tools, stains, mounting materials, raw specimens, books and notes.

address_history.commercial_address: Type Slide No. 1 / No. 2 + species names + price + named sales agents
address_history.workshop_address: custom cabinet drawers, fitted matrices, manuscript/printed specimen labels, locality/depth notes
address_history.diagnostic_feature: The commercial product identity survives inside a personal workshop archive: nineteenth-century sale language ('Type Slide No. 1/No. 2') is still physically present as drawer labels in the retained cabinet.

critical_guards: The Whipple narrative quotes a 1879 Belfast Naturalists' Field Club judgement; the contemporaneous BNA reports recovered by this project are dated April 1880. Preserve these as distinct dated source states rather than silently harmonising them.

The surviving Type Slide drawers identify product/workshop architecture, but the archive is believed to contain material remaining in Elcock's possession at death. Do not automatically call every surviving Type Slide a retail-sold copy returned from the market.
Catalogue/product labels are not unique-copy serial numbers. Product identity does not itself prove manufacture date or purchaser of an individual surviving slide.

Expedition names on surviving material establish source/provenance at the level supported by labels and catalogue description; do not infer a direct personal transfer from an expedition leader without separate documentation.
research_payoff: Elcock is now one of the strongest cases in the project for joining material preparation to commerce without treating the finished slide as the beginning of the story. Unlike Cole, whose fixed publication addresses survive despite replacement, Elcock preserves the workshop behind a commercial address: raw matter, tools and technique sit physically beside standardized priced products and dealer routes.
next_high_value_closure: Select one Type Slide from drawers 9-12 and transcribe its full printed/manuscript labels and numbered matrix. Test whether its species sequence can be matched to an advertisement, list, surviving duplicate, or buyer/institutional copy. Stop broad discovery unless a specific retail recipient or numbered counterpart appears.
